public.VOTE: S/PV.9461, p. 2. On 30 October 2023, the Council voted on United Kingdom draft S/2023/808. All 15 members voted in favour and the Council President announced unanimous adoption as resolution 2704 (2023).
public.OPERATIVE: Resolution 2704, operative paragraphs 1 and 2. The Council extended the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024. It expressed willingness to work with Colombia's Government on further extension of the mandate on the basis of agreement between the parties.
public.ADDITIONAL: Resolution 2704, final preambular paragraph. Resolution 2694 had already extended the Mission's role to monitoring and verification of the Government–ELN ceasefire. Resolution 2704 expressed willingness to consider Government–EMC monitoring and verification when the Secretary-General confirms a ceasefire with appropriate verification protocols and taking into account his update on implementation of resolution 2694.

Brazilian delegation source analyst.BRAZIL: S/PV.9461, p. 3. The presiding representative switched to speaking for Brazil. He said the Council should respond to Colombia's priorities as expressed by its Government and described the resolution as reflecting Colombia's sovereign will. Brazil supported the Government's total peace strategy and hoped the Council could authorize verification of the EMC ceasefire when sufficiently mature.

Ghanaian source analyst for the A3 state.A3: S/PV.9461, p. 2. Ghana spoke on behalf of the three African members. The A3 welcomed the unanimous mandate extension, supported Mission monitoring and verification in the EMC case contingent on the Secretary-General's conditions, and pledged to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter for Afro-Colombian and Indigenous people.

procedure: Gives the date, identifies United Kingdom draft S/2023/808 and records 15 votes in favour or unanimity.
renewal: Identifies resolution 2704 (2023) and extension of the existing UN Verification Mission mandate through 31 October 2024.
eln: Identifies existing ELN monitoring and verification authority under resolution 2694.
emc: Distinguishes willingness to consider Government–EMC verification from present authority and gives both the Secretary-General's confirmation of a ceasefire with appropriate protocols and the relevant implementation update.
further: States willingness to work with Colombia's Government on further extension based on agreement between the parties.
brazil_capacity: Distinguishes the national statement from the presidency and preserves Brazil's emphasis on priorities expressed by Colombia's Government.
brazil_hope: Gives Brazil's hope for later EMC authorization once the process is sufficiently mature.
a3_condition: Attributes the collective A3 statement to Ghana as speaker and records its support for EMC verification contingent on the Secretary-General's conditions.
a3_ethnic: Preserves the A3 commitment to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter for Afro-Colombian and Indigenous people.
common_ground: Identifies conditional future EMC verification as shared ground and explicitly separates these statements from a decision granting authority.

guards: No claim that the Council authorized Government–EMC verification in this resolution.
No confusion of the prior ELN authority with conditional EMC consideration.
No attribution of Brazil's rationale to the Council presidency, or conversion of national statements into a Council action.
No invented vote, opposition, consultation or other material statement.
contract: Maximum 185 words. Cite source IDs. Ten criteria at seven points each with independent material guards.
